title: The Real Cause of a Common Stroke May Have Been Missed for Decades
hook: A common type of stroke may not be mainly caused by fatty plaque after all — the strongest link was found with damaged small blood vessels deep in the brain.
key_points: Researchers found a common stroke type linked more strongly to damaged small brain blood vessels than to fatty plaque.
This challenges the long-standing assumption that plaque buildup is the main driver.
It helps explain why standard treatments like aspirin are often less effective for this stroke type.
The finding is pushing research toward therapies that target small blood vessels directly.
content_html: Doctors have long treated a common type of stroke as a plaque problem — fatty buildup narrowing the arteries that feed the brain. According to ScienceDaily, new research suggests that assumption may have been wrong for decades: the strongest link researchers found was with enlarged and damaged small blood vessels deep in the brain, not plaque.
extra_html: That distinction isn't just academic. It helps explain a puzzle doctors have long noticed — that standard treatments like aspirin, which make the most sense if plaque is the culprit, are often less effective for this stroke type than expected. If small, damaged blood vessels are the real driver, that mismatch starts to make sense, and it's now pushing researchers to search for therapies that target those tiny brain blood vessels directly rather than relying on plaque-focused approaches.

related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.
